title: Operation Lukavac 93: The Battle for Igman and the First NATO Ultimatum
content:
Operation Lukavac 93 opened on 2-3 July 1993. The VRS Main Staff assembled about 10,000 troops from the Sarajevo-Romanija and Herzegovina Corps, reinforced by the 65th Protection Motorized Regiment and 1st Guards Motorized Brigade. The first phase broke through at Rogoj, captured Trnovo, linked the two corps axes, and severed the ARBiH supply corridor to Gorazde. By 20 July the advance had reached the southeastern feet of Igman and Bjelasnica, where the battle paused as Bosnian Army defenses firmed.

On 31 July the VRS began the operation's final phase with a surprise attack on Mount Bjelasnica. Elements of the 65th Protection Regiment and 1st Guards then advanced across Bjelasnica and Igman during the next four days. The VRS reached the Veliko and Malo Polje area, placing Sarajevo's last overland supply link under immediate threat. The Bosnian Army reacted quickly: 1st Corps sent reinforcements through the airport tunnel and 3rd Corps dispatched elements of the 7th Muslim and 17th Krajina Mountain Brigades. By 5-6 August the defenders had consolidated on the main Igman mass while international pressure brought the offensive to a political-military decision point.

The UN demanded that the captured positions be vacated and secured against immediate re-entry, while NATO prepared an air-strike authorization if the strangulation of Sarajevo or attacks on other safe areas continued. At this point the historical operation record and the campaign choice must remain separate: the RS leadership still has to decide whether to comply or hold Igman, and the automatic NATO Council notice records pressure without deciding that question.
